item.title: Nov 04, 2026: Circle Q3 revenue up 17%, record stablecoins on Solana, Startale Card launches
item.description:
Circle reported third-quarter revenue and reserve income of $865 million, up 17%, and cut about 5% of its workforce. Stablecoins on Solana reached a record $17.51 billion, and Japan's Startale Group launched a card that spends its USDSC dollar stablecoin. Also: Democrats won both chambers of Congress, and the CFTC allowed single-stock perpetual futures.

  • Startale Group launches Startale Card for spending its USDSC stablecoin (Neweconomy)
  • Japanese car exporter SAT Japan accepts USDT and USDC from overseas buyers (bitbank)
  • Sony Bank says customer data leaked via unauthorized access at Securitize Japan (NADA NEWS)
  • Democrats win both chambers in U.S. midterms; Sherrod Brown wins in Ohio (CoinPost, The Block, NADA NEWS)
  • CFTC allows single-stock perpetual futures; Cboe- and Citadel-backed group sues (CoinPost, The Block, Crypto Times)
  • SEC staff view Canton Coin as a digital commodity in no-action letter (Neweconomy, The Block, Cointelegraph)
  • Follow-up: South Korea's ruling party formally proposes delaying the crypto income tax (The Block, bitbank, CoinDesk)
  • Justin Sun seeks about $264,000 in sanctions against World Liberty Financial (The Block, Neweconomy, Cointelegraph)
  • Hong Kong passes bill adopting the OECD Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework (bitbank)
  • Bhutan's Gelephu region to set up a central bank allowed to hold digital assets (CoinPost)
  • South Korea's president calls for a government-wide cybersecurity body after the Binance hack (CoinDesk)
  • Bitcoin falls to a seven-week low of $75,618, then rebounds above $78,000 (CoinDesk, CoinDesk, Cointelegraph)
  • Block's bitcoin gross profit halves; $764 million DOJ settlement agreed in principle (CoinPost, The Block, Crypto Times)
  • Riot Platforms sells 10,599 BTC in Q3, cutting holdings by about 79% (bitbank)
  • Follow-up: Morgan Stanley tokenizes U.S. stocks and Treasuries via DTCC's service (The Block, Crypto Times, bitbank)
  • Schroders tokenizes an emerging market bond strategy on Solana with Centrifuge (bitbank, CoinDesk)
  • Follow-up: objections to OKXICE tokenized stock trading reach 59 companies (Neweconomy, Crypto Times, CoinPost)
  • Cross River Bank to bring loan financing and transfers onto Arbitrum One (bitbank)
  • BitGo launches BitGo Global Markets for institutional trading and financing (The Block, bitbank)
  • Bullish picks Solana, Aptos and Ethereum for stock tokenization (Crypto Times, bitbank)
  • zERC20 launches v2 on mainnet with passkey browser accounts (Neweconomy, NADA NEWS)
  • Apple bans employees from prediction market trading on confidential information (bitbank, NADA NEWS)
  • Follow-up: Zcash grants committee withdraws plan to redirect 98,000 ZEC (CoinDesk)
  • Follow-up: Binance publishes initial incident report on the $6.3 billion hack (CoinPost, The Block, Crypto Times)
  • Follow-up: ZachXBT names Credit Mutuel Arkea as victim of $133 million theft (The Block, CoinPost, bitbank)
  • Follow-up: Mercado Bitcoin puts losses at $36.3 million, blocks $12.9 million (CoinPost, bitbank, Crypto Times)
  • BitMart reports a small hack possibly linked to the Mercado Bitcoin attackers (bitbank, Crypto Times)
  • Follow-up: GitBook says AI-agent attack accessed infrastructure credentials (CoinPost, bitbank, Crypto Times)
  • Follow-up: THORChain reopens trading; Binance attackers resume laundering (bitbank, CoinDesk, Cointelegraph)

item.title: Nov 01, 2026: Binance reopens withdrawals, FBI blames North Korea, THORChain halts on Ethereum reorg
item.description:
No major stablecoin headlines today. Binance began reopening withdrawals in phases and says about 95% of the loss is covered, and the FBI attributed the theft to North Korea. An Ethereum reorganization forced THORChain into an emergency pause, delaying laundering of the stolen funds, according to Chainalysis.

  • Three major crypto PACs spend about $170 million on the midterms, leaning Republican in the final stretch (bitbank, CoinDesk)
  • Crypto company political donations reach $233 million; Crypto.com gives $35 million to MAGA Inc., Public Citizen says (NADA NEWS)
  • Eurosystem publishes Appia consultation results without settling on a design (CRYPTO TIMES)
  • China's Communist Party to crack down on corruption that abuses crypto and blockchain (bitbank)
  • Objections to OKXICE tokenized stock trading reach 50 companies, including Nvidia, Micron and Nike (bitbank)
  • Tokenized stock onchain trading falls 39% in October as bStocks retakes first place from Robinhood, CoinDesk Research says (NADA NEWS)
  • Uber's tokenization pilot used HSBC tokenized deposits to buy a Franklin Templeton tokenized money market fund (NADA NEWS)
  • Trade[XYZ]'s new Anthropic-linked ANT contract falls about 20% in its first hour on Hyperliquid (CoinDesk)
  • Binance reopens withdrawals in phases and says about 95% of the loss is covered (bitbank, bitbank, Crypto Times)
  • Binance says ten major assets have reserve ratios of at least 100%; futures insurance fund used (Crypto Times, Cointelegraph, bitbank)
  • FBI attributes the Binance theft to North Korea and asks the industry to block related addresses (NADA NEWS, bitbank, CoinDesk)
  • Ethereum reorg forces THORChain into an emergency pause, delaying laundering of stolen funds, Chainalysis says (bitbank, Crypto Times)
  • North Korean hackers move about $38 million through Relay Protocol in seven hours, Specter says (bitbank)
  • Binance has no cyber insurance and SAFU has no outside insurance behind it, The Insurer reports (NADA NEWS)

item.title: Oct 31, 2026: Binance attacker skirts stablecoin freezes via Tron lending, Tether profit and reserves, Elliptic on USDT swaps
item.description:
The Binance attacker used lending on Tron to get around stablecoin freezes, according to Chainalysis. Tether posted $1.5 billion in third quarter net operating profit, with excess reserves nearly doubling, and Elliptic put new numbers on the attacker's USDT swaps into Ether.

  • Tether's Q3 net operating profit hits $1.5 billion as excess reserves nearly double to $7.95 billion (CoinPost, bitbank, Crypto Times)
  • Binance attacker used lending on Tron to get around stablecoin freezes, Chainalysis says (The Block)
  • Attacker swapped about 434 million USDT into 160,451 ETH at prices 12 to 26 percent worse than market, Elliptic says (CRYPTO TIMES)
  • Dispute over when issuers can freeze funds as Sen. Lummis cites the Clarity bill (CoinPost, The Block)
  • Binance Japan resumes crypto deposits while withdrawals stay suspended (CRYPTO TIMES)
  • President Trump says the government is looking into North Korean involvement in the Binance hack (CoinPost, NADA NEWS, Crypto Times)
  • CFTC Chair Selig says the Binance hack backs up the case for its crypto market proposals (CoinPost, NADA NEWS, Crypto Times)
  • Digital Chamber urges Congress to pass a narrow exchange oversight and customer protection bill (Crypto Times, CoinPost)
  • ICE deletes X post on Trade[XYZ] partnership and reposts it stating regulatory approval is required (Crypto Times, bitbank)
  • a16z, DeFi Education Fund and Uniswap Labs ask Illinois to keep DEXs out of the broker definition (Crypto Times)
  • Bitcoin trades near $77,000 as October heads for a 7.7 percent drop (bitbank, Crypto Times, CRYPTO TIMES)
  • US spot Bitcoin ETFs see $643 million in net outflows on October 30 (bitbank, Crypto Times)
  • Crypto stocks close lower with Coinbase down 10.62 percent (CoinPost)
  • Next Technology authorizes selling or borrowing against about 5,833 BTC (CoinDesk, bitbank)
  • Bank of Japan to raise ETF sales to about 860 billion yen a year at book value from January 2027 (CRYPTO TIMES)
  • Hyperliquid earned about $105 million in September as core fees fall to 64 percent of revenue, Grayscale says (CoinPost, bitbank)
  • Uber tests tokenization with HSBC and Franklin Templeton (CoinDesk)
  • MetaMask adds native Stellar support (CRYPTO TIMES)

item.title: Oct 26, 2026: Canada's no-interest stablecoin rules, Anchorpoint's retail delay, Circle Match
item.description:
Canada opens a consultation on draft stablecoin rules that keep a ban on paying interest to holders; Standard Chartered's Anchorpoint declines to commit to a retail launch date in Hong Kong; Circle launches hourly auctions that pair USDC issuance and redemption for institutions. Plus the GMO Internet extortion demand, Sony-backed Soneium's token plan, bitcoin back below 80,000 dollars before the Fed, and the Electrum fee-bump bug.

  • Canada opens consultation on draft stablecoin rules and keeps the ban on paying interest to holders (CoinDesk)
  • Anchorpoint, the Standard Chartered-led Hong Kong dollar stablecoin venture, will not commit to a retail launch date (Cointelegraph, bitbank)
  • Circle launches Circle Match, hourly auctions pairing institutional USDC issuance and redemption orders (CRYPTO TIMES)
  • GMO Internet breach: a person claiming responsibility demands 1 million dollars; group shares fall as much as 11% (CRYPTO TIMES, CRYPTO TIMES)
  • Soneium, the Sony joint venture's Ethereum layer two, announces plans for a SONEIUM token (CoinPost, Neweconomy, bitbank)
  • South Korea's presidential office says a fourth crypto tax delay is under review but not decided (Neweconomy, CoinPost, The Block)
  • California's financial regulator asks the SEC to drop a provision removing state pre-sale review (NADA NEWS)
  • MEXC phases out service in the Netherlands, citing the lack of a MiCA license (bitbank)
  • Bitcoin slips below 80,000 dollars again before the Fed meeting; US spot ETFs took in about 301 million dollars last week (CoinDesk, Cointelegraph, NADA NEWS)
  • Strategy pauses bitcoin purchases after five weeks and buys back about 205 million dollars of STRC preferred shares (The Block, bitbank)
  • Strive buys 6,182 bitcoin, lifting holdings to 43,000 (The Block, bitbank)
  • Aviva Investors lists a tokenized share class of its sterling liquidity fund on the XRP Ledger with Ripple (The Block, Cointelegraph, bitbank)
  • Tether says 15 mining firms, including Bitmain, MicroBT and Canaan, will support its open-source mining kit MDK (CRYPTO TIMES)
  • Hong Kong names Nasdaq-listed Solana Company a strategic enterprise (Cointelegraph, bitbank)
  • Lido opens validators of up to 2,048 ETH to any operator with its 0x02 CSM (CRYPTO TIMES)
  • The eCash hard fork of bitcoin is set for around October 29th, with a 1-for-1 ECX airdrop (Crypto Times)
  • Electrum fixes a bug that let rogue servers steal funds when users raised a transaction fee (CoinDesk)
  • SlowMist finds more than 1,500 phishing sites tied to the DarkSword attack on iPhones (CoinPost, Neweconomy, NADA NEWS)
  • Solana trading bot BloomTrading loses about 954,000 dollars from 49 wallets and promises full refunds (Crypto Times)
  • Foundation traces phishing emails to Passport wallet users to compromised Cloudflare API keys (Crypto Times, bitbank)
  • Keystone customers say the breach exposed order data the company promised to delete after 180 days (The Block)
  • Bithumb and Upbit flag INIT as high risk after Initia's 2.7 million dollar exploit (Crypto Times)
